title.t: A recorded commission differs from the contract

when.t: The authorized user enters a commission dispute: the recorded figure, the contract's figure and the clause.

steps.t: If the two figures differ, Agent 15 raises a legal-line alert quoting the clause word for word. It changes no figure.
Separately, after every close Agent 15 compares its commission with the amount Agent 14 logged and raises the same kind of alert if they differ.
This reaches Agent 15 only as the authorized user's signed setting; nothing reads a contract or a statement.

you_see.t: A legal-line alert with the recorded figure and the clause (the contract figure itself is not in the alert).

test.t: Recorded 36,000; contract figure 27,000; clause "Seller shall pay a total commission of 6% of the sale price at closing."

title.t: An expense fits two categories with different tax treatment

when.t: An expense is entered with more than one category and differing tax flags.

steps.t: Agent 15 records it with both categories and both flags, marked as a conflict for the accountant; it picks neither.
The mark appears in the profit-and-loss report.

never.t: Choose the category or the tax treatment.

you_see.t: The expense in the report, marked with the conflict.

test.t: Home office internet, 90, categories office and utilities, flags deductible 100% and deductible partial.

title.t: Two sources claim the same result

when.t: A second attribution claim for the same result arrives from a different source.

steps.t: Agent 15 sends the authorized user a report listing both claims; it picks neither.

test.t: Facebook ads and a past-client referral each claim the T1 sale (12,000).

title.t: A month of data is missing

when.t: A profit-and-loss report is asked for months not marked as received.

steps.t: Agent 15 lists those months as missing; nothing is filled in.
A month counts as received only when the authorized user marks it so.
The report lists the commissions and expenses on record; it computes no totals.

you_see.t: A report naming the missing months.

test.t: August is marked received; a report for August and September is asked for.

when.t: The authorized user passes on a question about commission wording.

steps.t: Agent 15 raises a legal-line alert with the question; it does not answer.
This reaches Agent 15 only as the authorized user's signed setting; nothing reads a contract or a statement.

you_see.t: A legal-line alert quoting the question.

test.t: "Does the co-op split in paragraph 4 apply to a dual agency sale?"

title.t: A commission depends on an unsigned document

when.t: A close arrives from Agent 07 with the settlement statement not signed.

steps.t: Agent 15 keeps the commission labeled as a projection, not a recorded figure.
With no commission amount on the close, it computes one at the default 8% of the sale price and labels it computed.
A close with neither an amount nor a sale price records no amount.

never.t: Present a projection as a recorded commission.

you_see.t: A report showing 36,000 labeled a projection, computed at the default rate.

test.t: Closing October 20; an unsigned settlement statement with a sale price of 450,000 arrives; a report is asked for.

when.t: An expense is entered with no receipt on file.

steps.t: Agent 15 records it as unverified.
Nothing changes it later: there is no step that marks an expense verified after entry.

never.t: Treat an old unverified expense as verified.

you_see.t: The expense in the report marked unverified.

test.t: Open house signs, 140, no receipt; a daily run; then a report.

when.t: A pipeline value is asked for over leads that include unknown-tier leads.

steps.t: Agent 15 leaves out the leads marked UNKNOWN, totals the rest, counts the ones left out and says so. (A lead with no tier, or a tier spelled differently, is counted in.)
The leads and their values come in the request itself.

you_see.t: A total of 30,000 with one unknown lead left out.

title.t: A disbursement instruction arrives by email

when.t: Text passed to Agent 15 mentions a disbursement.

steps.t: Agent 15 raises a legal-line alert: disbursements go only through a voice-verified process run by a person.

Text anywhere in the setting, nested fields included, that contains "earnest money", "trust account", "escrow" or "wire the funds" raises a legal-line alert as out of scope; "disbursement" raises one as a wire-adjacent instruction for a voice-verified person. Nothing is recorded (fixed 2026-10-28: a mention inside a nested field was not caught).
The authorized user passes the email on as a signed setting; that is the only way text reaches Agent 15.

you_see.t: A legal-line alert quoting the instruction.

test.t: "Disbursement instruction from the title company: please wire the funds to the new account below."

title.t: A forecast is asked for beyond the data

when.t: A forecast is asked for further ahead than the data covers.

steps.t: Agent 15 declines the longer horizon and says how far the data goes.
The report carries no forecast figures, only the horizons.
A request without a horizon gets a question instead. (A missing data horizon counts as 0 months, so such a request is declined, not asked about.)

never.t: Forecast past what the data supports.

you_see.t: A report saying 12 months was declined and 6 is what the data supports.

test.t: A 12-month forecast with 6 months of data; then a request with no horizon.
